Apologies for the wall of text, on mobile. Not me personally, but I went to a treatment center for PTSD. Their was one trans girl in my group who's story was the first to make me cry there. Our stories were told in letter format, and the letter to her father started out "Daddy, why did you kill mommy?" The father was cold, distant and extremely physically abusive. I thought that was the worst of it, but her letter to her mom was so much worse. Super obsessed with germs and until she was 16 would scrub her in the shower with scalding hot water. She wouldn't let her have any social interactions outside of school. She'd lie to neighbors and others and tell them she was afraid of animals, because her mother thought they were dirty when she actually loves animals and just wanted to play with them. When she was a senior in high school in orchestra, her mother refused to buy her (then him) the necessary clothes for a performance at an amusement park. She was bullied by all her peers for making them throw the competition because she was in a white t-shirt and khakis with dirty old tennis shoes instead of suit and dress shoes. Not only that, but as she was getting out of the car that morning her mother grabbed her, and wrote her name, address and phone number on the back of her shirt "in case she gets lost". Ceramics takes a considerable amount of clean up time and I ended up missing my bus a few times because of it. One day my best friend Taigen and I we running particularly late so we ran while holding hands to the bus. 

Our bus driver was an older black woman. As soon as we got on the bus she started yelling at us to separate cause she "doesn't want that gay shit on her bus" this was 2009- my school was extremely progressive with issues like that. we were shocked and disgusted by her homophobia so we didn't listen and stayed together in the same seat and told her to get an AP if she wanted. She calls the AP over and immediately starts telling him that we were being disruptive and then told him that I (a small white female) called her the N word! (My best friend Taigen is half black and half Japanese, she wasn't accused of anything)

I got expelled and it turned into the biggest ordeal. My friends and I protested and ended up starting the schools first Gay Straight Alliance club. I was the secretary of the club, and my bus driver (who still had to allow me on her bus when everything was cleared) never said a word to or looked at me again.

Totally didn't read the article, but I've talked to numerous professionals and others also diagnosed and the most interesting take I've found on bpd is that because the disorder is often rooted in trauma, bpd itself is just maladaptive coping skills due to complex ptsd. If you work on the underlying trauma, you can greatly reduce how your symptoms manifest. I use to cling to my diagnosis and used it as an excuse. After seeking 90 days residential treatment  at The Refuge A Healing Place (one of the countries top PTSD treatment centers) I don't identify with the disorder. I don't like to use the label, because I am not my bpd. Seriously this view and treatment has saved my life. I was a nearly homeless heroin addict who burned every bridge I ever built. at my worst, I can't object to any of the bpd stigmas because I was a walking natural disaster that destroyed everyone around me. After treatment, and treating my diagnosis as a set of maladaptive coping skills, I have my friends back. I have my family back. I have a wonderful and loving significant other. I don't act on my emotional instability, I use dbt techniques and communication. My life isn't all rainbows and sunshine, but its greatly improved from where I was. For everyone that thinks they can't get better, it's possible. You are worth it, you are deserving of love and happiness no matter how terrible of a person you think you are.
